summary: 638 Produce items, but the depth is almost all cultivar/variety children (e.g. 18 apple cultivars, 13 mango cultivars, 11 date cultivars) hung off ~120 real root items. That makes the category look huge while leaving big everyday and global gaps. The single biggest gap: FRESH culinary herbs and aromatics are entirely absent from Produce (cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, dill, oregano, thyme, rosemary, sage, tarragon, chives-as-herb, etc. all live only in 'Spices & Herbs' as dried) even though recipes call for them as fresh produce with short fridge life. Citrus is thin (no mandarin/clementine/tangerine/satsuma); there is no generic 'chili pepper', no cassava/yuca, no edamame, no cherry/grape tomato as a real item, no gooseberry. Whole continents of common produce are missing: African greens (sukuma wiki/collards-as-greens, callaloo/amaranth, molokhia, cowpea & pumpkin leaves, managu/spider plant), Southeast Asian gourds & aromatics (bitter melon, bottle/snake/ridge gourd, luffa, winter melon, banana blossom, water spinach/kangkong, choy sum, gai lan, tatsoi, galangal exists but fingerroot/krachai, curry leaf, kaffir lime leaf, pandan, Thai basil, holy basil, shiso/perilla all missing as produce), Latin/Caribbean (chayote exists but no fresh epazote, no breadfruit, no soursop/guanabana, no mamey, no green papaya called out), and many fruits (rambutan, mangosteen, durian, soursop, custard apple/sugar apple, feijoa, loquat, tamarillo, physalis/cape gooseberry, mulberry, elderberry, lingonberry, sea buckthorn, pawpaw). Well-formedness is mostly OK on storage/freshness/tags (every item has freshnessByStorage + defaultStorage), but there is a systemic naming-convention defect: ~70 items use inverted 'noun adjective' display names ('carrot orange', 'cabbage red', 'beet red', 'kiwi green', 'tomato yellow') instead of natural 'adjective noun'. There is also a real data bug: the id 'pineapple' is actually a QUINCE variety ('pineapple quince') parented to quince, and genuine pineapple (Ananas comosus) cultivars (md-2, queen, red-spanish, smooth-cayenne) are mis-parented onto it, so the tropical fruit pineapple has no correct root entry. Redundancies: two self-duplicating children (cantaloupe-cantaloupe, scallion-scallion) and a family of placeholder '*-standard' children that just mirror their parent.
issues: FRESH HERBS MISSING FROM PRODUCE: cilantro/coriander, parsley, basil (incl. Thai/holy/lemon), mint, dill, oregano, thyme, rosemary, sage, tarragon, marjoram, chervil, savory exist only in 'Spices & Herbs' (dried framing). Fresh-bunch herbs are produce-aisle items with ~7-14 day fridge life and recipes constantly call for 'fresh cilantro/basil/parsley'. This is the category's largest comprehensiveness gap.

DATA BUG / id collision: item id 'pineapple' is NOT pineapple - its name is 'pineapple quince' and parentIds=['quince'] (Cydonia oblonga, a quince cultivar). Genuine pineapple (Ananas comosus) cultivars md-2, queen, red-spanish, smooth-cayenne are parented to 'pineapple' and therefore sit under quince. The tropical fruit pineapple has no correct top-level entry. Names 'perola pineapple quince', 'queen pineapple quince', 'sugarloaf pineapple quince' are mangled (these are pineapple cultivars, not quinces).

Systemic naming defect: ~70 variety items use inverted 'noun adjective' display names instead of natural English. Examples: 'carrot orange'->'orange carrot', 'cabbage red'->'red cabbage', 'beet red'->'red beet', 'kiwi green'->'green kiwi', 'tomato yellow'->'yellow tomato', 'kohlrabi purple'->'purple kohlrabi', 'currant black'->'black currant', 'guava red'->'red guava'. Hurts search/display.

Citrus is under-built: no mandarin, clementine, tangerine, satsuma, blood orange, navel orange, or even a plain 'orange' root (only lemon, lime, grapefruit, kumquat exist). Very common everyday + global (Morocco/France/Mediterranean) gap.

No generic 'chili pepper' / 'chile' root and no Thai bird's-eye chili, no Kashmiri chili, no aji amarillo, no piri piri, no Hungarian wax - specific chiles (anaheim, poblano, serrano, habanero, scotch bonnet, etc.) exist under 'pepper' but the global chili palette is thin and there is no umbrella 'chili pepper' people would search.

No cassava/yuca/manioc, no edamame, no fava/broad bean as fresh produce (fava exists only as dried 'Legumes & Beans'), no long bean/yardlong, no runner bean, no winged bean - all common globally (Africa, Asia, Latin America).

No cherry tomato or grape tomato as findable items: 'grape' id is 'grape tomato' and 'pear' id is 'pear tomato', but there is no 'cherry tomato' and the table grape (Vitis) fruit itself is entirely MISSING - there is no grape fruit item at all (the id 'grape' is a tomato).

Large global fruit gaps: rambutan, mangosteen, durian, soursop (guanabana), custard apple / sugar apple (sweetsop), sapodilla, mamey sapote, feijoa (pineapple guava), loquat, medlar, jujube, tamarillo, physalis/cape gooseberry, gooseberry (Ribes), mulberry, elderberry, lingonberry, sea buckthorn, salak, pawpaw, ackee (Caribbean/Jamaica), breadfruit (Caribbean/Pacific).

African leafy-greens gap: no callaloo/amaranth greens, no molokhia (jute mallow / Egyptian spinach), no cowpea leaves, no pumpkin leaves, no managu (African nightshade), no spider plant (saga/dek), no cassava leaves, and 'collard green' is not surfaced as 'sukuma wiki' (Kenya/East Africa).

Southeast/South Asian gap: no bitter melon (bitter gourd/karela), bottle gourd (lauki/calabash), snake gourd, ridge gourd, luffa, ash/wax gourd (winter melon), tinda, ivy gourd, pointed gourd (parwal), drumstick/moringa pods, banana blossom/flower, heart of palm, water spinach (kangkong/ong choy), choy sum, gai lan (chinese broccoli exists, gai lan alias would help), tatsoi; aromatics: fingerroot/krachai, curry leaf, kaffir lime leaf, pandan, fresh turmeric, fresh wasabi, horseradish (fresh root), galangal exists but only galangal varieties.
Self-duplicating children: 'cantaloupe-cantaloupe' (name 'cantaloupe', parent cantaloupe) and 'scallion-scallion' (name 'scallion', parent scallion) are pure duplicates of their parents.

Placeholder '*-standard' children mirror their parent with no varietal meaning: arugula-standard, broccolini-standard, celeriac-standard, green-bean-standard, jerusalem-artichoke-standard, jicama-standard, leek-standard, watercress-standard.

Mushroom dietaryTags inconsistency: 'lobster mushroom' and 'oyster mushroom' (and 'brown turkey fig') are missing Vegan + Vegetarian tags - their names contain 'lobster'/'oyster'/'turkey' but they are vegan produce.

'coconut' is missing the Nut-Free tag (it's tagged Vegan/Vegetarian/Gluten-Free/Dairy-Free only). Coconut is a drupe, not a true nut, but it is a recognized tree-nut allergen for labeling - flag for a deliberate decision either way; current state is just inconsistent with every other Produce item.
'easter egg radish' is missing the Vegan tag (has Vegetarian/GF/DF/Nut-Free but not Vegan) - clearly an oversight for a radish.

Mislabeled/odd names: 'celeriac celery' and 'celeriac celery standard' (celeriac is not celery - should be 'celeriac' / 'celery root'); 'celery red'/'celery golden' should be 'red celery'/'golden celery'; 'turnip green' has parent='-' while 'beet green' also parent='-' yet most greens are children - inconsistent parenting of leafy by-products.
'jack-o-lantern' (carving pumpkin) is parented to pumpkin but pumpkin itself is parented to squash; fine, but jack-o-lantern is not culinary - low value, not a defect per se.

Storage note: dates and tamarind use Refrigerated [365,730] which is correct for dried but their defaultStorage should arguably be Pantry (dried dates/tamarind are pantry-stable); worth confirming, not necessarily wrong.
redundancies: cantaloupe-cantaloupe is a child named 'cantaloupe' duplicating its own parent 'cantaloupe' - delete the child
scallion-scallion is a child named 'scallion' duplicating its own parent 'scallion' - delete the child

'green onion scallion' (id green-onion) and 'spring onion scallion' (id spring-onion) are both children of scallion that are really just the SAME thing as the parent scallion; collapse green onion / spring onion into aliases of scallion rather than separate children
'arugula standard' is a placeholder child identical to parent arugula - remove or rename to a real cultivar

'watercress standard' placeholder duplicates parent watercress; also 'upland-cress' is named 'upland cress watercress' yet a separate 'upland' cress exists under 'cress' - overlapping watercress/cress trees
'green bean standard' placeholder duplicates parent green-bean
'celeriac celery standard' placeholder duplicates parent celeriac (which is itself misnamed 'celeriac celery')
'jerusalem artichoke standard' placeholder duplicates parent jerusalem-artichoke; note 'sunchoke' alias missing entirely
'tenderstem broccolini' and 'broccolini standard' / 'organic broccolini' all overlap; tenderstem is a brand/regional (UK) name for broccolini - make it an alias not a sibling cultivar

id 'pineapple' is actually 'pineapple quince' under quince; 'perola pineapple quince', 'queen pineapple quince', 'sugarloaf pineapple quince', 'md-2', 'red-spanish', 'smooth-cayenne' are genuine pineapple (Ananas) cultivars mis-parented to this quince - they need a real pineapple root, not quince lineage
